overview: This joint resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act, a law that lets Congress cancel recent federal rules by a simple majority vote, to overturn a Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) policy published March 3, 2025, titled "Policy on Adhering to the Text of the Administrative Procedure Act." That policy ended the department's longstanding voluntary practice of taking public comment on certain decisions, such as those involving grants, benefits and contracts, even where the law does not require it. The Government Accountability Office concluded in August 2025 that the policy counts as a rule that Congress can review. Had it passed both chambers and been signed, the policy would have had no force or effect. It failed in the Senate on a 50-50 vote on December 18, 2025.
for: Supporters say the public should keep its chance to comment on HHS decisions that affect health programs, grants and benefits, and that dropping it reduces transparency.
against: Critics say the policy simply follows what the Administrative Procedure Act actually requires and lets the department act more quickly without extra steps the law never demanded.
